code.originalText: Six-week review after the dose changes: electrolytes, renin, repeat thyroid tests, and back pain

text.paragraph: Six-week review after the dose changes: electrolytes, renin, repeat thyroid tests, and back pain. [S]

Mr. Kennedy returns six weeks after hydrocortisone was reduced to 10, 5 and 5 mg and fludrocortisone raised to 0.1 mg, and three weeks after the influenza, during which he doubled his hydrocortisone for four days and then went back to his usual dose; the illness settled without vomiting or any emergency. His energy now lasts the day. The salt craving and the lightheadedness on standing have gone. He has gained 2 kg. He feels a little slow and cold in the mornings. He has had six physical therapy sessions; his back aches less and he wears the brace only in the car. [S]

list.item:
Primary adrenal insufficiency (autoimmune Addison's disease) (E27.1). Well replaced on 20 mg hydrocortisone and 0.1 mg fludrocortisone: sodium 139, potassium 4.4 mmol/L, creatinine 0.94 mg/dL, plasma renin activity 2.6 ng/mL/h in the upper normal range, no postural drop. He used the sick-day rules correctly during influenza. [S]
Continue the same doses.
Electrolytes and renin at the nine-month review.

Autoimmune hypothyroidism (E06.3). TSH 9.2 mIU/L, up from 7.4 two months ago, with free T4 0.8 ng/dL at the lower limit and positive thyroid peroxidase antibodies: autoimmune hypothyroidism, confirmed on repeat, with mild symptoms. As part of an autoimmune polyglandular syndrome it is likely to progress. Glucocorticoid replacement is secure, so thyroid hormone can safely be started (starting it first can bring on an adrenal crisis). Dr. Desai agrees. [S]
Start levothyroxine 50 mcg each morning, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast and apart from calcium or iron.
TSH and free T4 in six weeks.

Raised TSH with positive thyroid peroxidase antibodies (R94.6). Confirmed on repeat and now recorded as autoimmune hypothyroidism; this finding is closed. [S]
Followed under autoimmune hypothyroidism.

Influenza A (J10.1). Resolved without complications. [S]
Influenza vaccine again in the autumn.

Chronic low back pain after lumbar disc surgery (M96.1). Improving with exercise therapy: Oswestry 26% from 32%. [S]
Continue physical therapy and swimming.
Brace for the car only.
